Natural capacitor voltage balancing dynamics of flying capacitor converter when supplied to an induction motor can be analyzed using a linear state space motor model, which requires the mid frequency impedance of the motor to be known.
the natural capacitor voltage balancing behavior of a three phase Flying Capacitor Converter (FCC) is degraded at low motor speeds and that a balance-boosting filter can improve the dynamic response.
the dynamic response of the flying capacitor converter drive is significantly improved by using the proposed balance booster filter, and that this improvement is more pronounced at low speeds.

the design of the control system for a flying capacitor (FC) based converter.
the development of new methods and algorithms for the control of electric machines and power converters, and the analysis of their dynamic behavior.

the natural voltage balancing is not good enough for the converter to be used for induction motor drives.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method is a very effective and practical approach to solve the voltage balancing problem for a flying capacitor inverter, and the proposed method is also applicable to other PWM inverters with capacitors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the voltage balance dynamics are highly dependent on motor speed, and that the balance dynamics are not necessarily the same at different speeds.
the natural balancing behavior of a flying capacitor converter supplying an induction motor is significantly worse than for a purely resistive load.

the dynamic behavior of the flying capacitor converter is highly sensitive to the motor impedance at low frequencies, and that a low impedance motor will improve the dynamic behavior of this type of converter.
